nodes.label: D2: Hybrid model — push/callback canonical, async-iterator layered on top
nodes.rationale: §24/§15.4 require transport-oriented, low-allocation callbacks; the pull adapter keeps for-await ergonomics without forcing event-object allocation on push consumers.

nodes.label: D3: Sync calls + async checkpoints (backpressure at element/fragment boundaries)
nodes.rationale: A promise on every value()/startElement() would fight the allocation-free hot path; the generator awaits only at top-level element boundaries and binary-fragment emission, matching existing awaitDrain usage.

nodes.label: D4: Binary = fragment sub-stream + bulkDataReference event
nodes.rationale: §33 requires fragment boundaries preservable for lossless encapsulated writers; a single-buffer value() event collapses boundaries and pushes toward eager materialization.

nodes.label: D5: File Meta Information as leading bracketed sub-stream
nodes.rationale: Emitted first so a listener knows the transfer syntax before the main dataset arrives; replaces the ad-hoc fmi field.

nodes.label: D6: Optional sourceSpan {start,end} baked into structural events
nodes.rationale: The passthrough writer needs it; retrofitting later would be a breaking vocabulary change — the one deliberate forward-looking concession.

nodes.label: D9: Decode core trapped in readFileLazy closures — scoped walker now, extract core later
nodes.rationale: materializeElement/resolveVrInstance/charset setup were closures inside readFileLazy; faithful reuse meant re-deriving 30-40% of the lazy core, converging with extraction — so ship the common path with delegation and schedule the shared-core extraction (became Slice J). Also: isBinary() is true for numeric VRs, so routing is by decoded value type, not isBinary().

nodes.label: D12: Default cardinality-violation policy warnAndPreserve; SQ VM constrains attribute occurrence not item count
nodes.rationale: A literal reading of §12 would warn on every multi-frame object; violations apply only to non-sequence scalar VRs exceeding declared VM. Violations exposed on listener.violations — later generalized as the slice-H diagnostic channel.

nodes.label: D13: PN proxy shape — component object with non-enumerable toString/toJSON
nodes.rationale: VM 1 → the {Alphabetic, Ideographic, Phonetic} object itself so .Alphabetic works directly; reuses pnAddValueAccessors (non-enumerable, so cross-source structural equality is unaffected).

nodes.label: D14: Precision/raw retention via optional rawValue on the value event (round-trip-based)
nodes.rationale: IS is capped at 12 chars so it never overflows JS safe integers; the real string-retention case is DS (≤16 chars) whose double can drop the final digit — hence a VR-agnostic round-trip check, not a VR-specific rule.

nodes.label: D15: Part 10 event writer layers over canonical DicomDict.write, not a second encoder
nodes.rationale: DicomMessage.write is already the canonical byte-faithful encoder; a streaming event encoder would duplicate it, with the only added benefit being not buffering during write — a niche need, deferred until real.

nodes.label: D16: Byte identity — body-level guarantee already shipped on lazy+passthrough path
nodes.rationale: Steve Pieper's 'unedited parts unchanged' ask is already delivered body byte-for-byte by the dirty-tracking passthrough writer; remaining gaps are meta-group re-encode, deflate wrapper bytes, and the event/naturalized path — the last being exactly what dicom-curate needs.

nodes.label: D19: Oracle = pieper/dicompare cross-toolkit harness; corpus from IDC + phantom generator
nodes.rationale: Parity measured against an independent parser, not dcmjs's own current output, so current bugs are not pinned as the contract; PHI-bearing weird data reproduced structurally by an automated phantom generator.

nodes.label: D20: Conformance validation layer (slice H) — validator as one more event-stream listener
D21: Normalization as opt-in transform (slice I) — loss-correction kept out of preserve-first core
nodes.rationale: Folding correction into the naturalizer would reintroduce §3.1 source-dependent-output drift; normalize as a separately-versioned transform between source and sink, applied only on request.

nodes.label: D22: Machine-readable schema of the naturalized representation
D23: Part 10 never forces whole-header buffering (tag ordering guarantees)
nodes.rationale: FMI first, charset and private creators precede their dependents by tag order, BOT sits at the start of encapsulated data, functional groups precede Pixel Data — the one genuine look-ahead case is unordered DICOMweb JSON, bounded by the enclosing item. Streaming's real payoff is pixel payloads and starting before the last byte, not header size.

nodes.label: D25: Adopt dicom-curate as the canonical curation/de-identification layer
nodes.rationale: dicom-curate is already a dcmjs read-modify-write consumer pinned to 0.51.1, encoding workarounds for exactly the defects 1.0 fixes (VM-collapse shape, private-creator loss, raw-value drop, separate metaheader handling); migrating it onto the new contract lets those workarounds be deleted and makes it the flagship real-world consumer.

nodes.label: D27: Rule catalog as the one source of truth; TS and JSON-Schema as derived projections
nodes.rationale: One normative encoding; every consumer is a projection or reader of it, so agreement is by construction — literal JSON Schema rejected because it cannot express VM patterns like 3-3n and is built for materialized-document validation, not element-by-element streams.
